title: Circuit Judge, 11th Judicial Circuit, Group 69
what_it_does: Circuit judges hear felony criminal cases, major civil suits, family and probate matters. This seat is elected by voters across the 11th Circuit (Miami-Dade). Nonpartisan; a candidate needs a majority, and this contest was not decided in August.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); both candidates are marked Qualified, which for a nonpartisan seat means the August vote did not produce a majority winner (or the seat is decided only in November). Positions have not been researched; check the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

candidates.name: Rita Baez
candidates.occupation: Personal injury lawyer in private practice, Miami-Dade County
candidates.background: Baez is a personal injury lawyer in private practice in Miami-Dade County. A 2026 Miami-Dade judicial voter guide reports she has about 30 years in practice, including nine years as an assistant state attorney, and has tried roughly 80 civil jury trials. She led the August 18, 2026 primary for 11th Circuit Group 69 with 37.1% and advanced to the November 3 runoff against Bonita Jones-Peabody.

record.item: About 30 years in practice, including nine years as an assistant state attorney; roughly 80 civil jury trials. The voter guide called her 'a credible candidate' while preferring another contender on experience.

candidates.name: Bonita Jones-Peabody
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Attorney in private practice; former assistant public defender, Miami-Dade Public Defender's Office
candidates.background: Jones-Peabody has more than 35 years in practice, spending many years at the Miami-Dade Public Defender's Office, where she was a senior supervising attorney handling serious felony cases and mentoring newer lawyers, before moving into a varied private practice covering criminal, civil, family, juvenile, probate, immigration and personal injury matters. A 2026 Miami-Dade judicial voter guide credits her with more than 200 criminal jury trials. She founded the nonprofit Education Means More Access and serves on bar association and civic boards including the League of Women Voters and the Gwen S. Cherry Black Women Lawyers Association.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

record.item: More than 35 years in practice and more than 200 criminal jury trials; described by a 2026 Miami-Dade judicial voter guide as an experienced criminal defense lawyer with many years at the Public Defender's Office.
